question: When you profiled the round-7 frame, how was GPU time divided between the path-tracing dispatch and the pass that adds up each pixel's samples?
answer: In the round-7 frame (512x512, 64 spp, default scene) the split is essentially all trace: I instrumented the host with a PT_SPLIT knob that commits the trace command buffer separately so Metal reports its own GPUStartTime/GPUEndTime, and the sample-parallel trace dispatch measured 30.30 ms of GPU time while the combine pass (summing each pixel's spp samples in order, tone mapping, writing the image) measured 0.42 ms — about 98.6% vs 1.4%. That is why I stopped attacking per-sample buffer traffic (the buffer is already sample-major, so the 32 lanes of a simdgroup write contiguous memory) and concentrated on the BVH-walk cost inside the trace kernel; the depth sweep (1/2/3/12 depth = 5.82/10.96/17.10/30.28 ms) and the shadow-walk disable (26.68 ms, so shadow rays are only 3.65 ms) both point at closest-hit traversal ALU/latency as the dominant cost.

question: When you profiled the round-7 frame, how was GPU time divided between the path-tracing dispatch and the pass that adds up each pixel's samples?
answer: The split is about 99:1 in favour of the path-tracing dispatch. I measured it by adding a debug knob (PT_SPLIT=1) to a scratch copy of the round-7 code that submits the trace dispatch and the sample-combining pass as two separate command buffers, so Metal's own GPUStartTime/GPUEndTime report each one separately. At the benchmark setting (512x512, 64 spp, scene-default) the trace dispatch took 30.30 ms of GPU time and the combine pass took 0.42 ms — i.e. tracing is ~98.6% of the GPU time and the summing/tone-mapping pass is ~1.4%, and the two add up to the ~30.7 ms gpu_ms_best of the round-7 candidate. That is why I treated the sample-buffer traffic and the combine kernel as not worth attacking this round, and spent the effort on the traversal loop instead (lane-footprint remaps, stack layout, threadgroup shape).

question: When you profiled the round-7 frame, how was GPU time divided between the path-tracing dispatch and the pass that adds up each pixel's samples?
answer:
Round-7 frame GPU split, measured at 512x512 / 64 spp on the default scene: the path-tracing dispatch took 30.30 ms and the sample-combining pass took 0.42 ms, i.e. the trace kernel is 98.6% of the GPU time and the combine pass is 1.4% (the whole frame's gpu_ms_best was 30.706 ms).

How I know: I built a throwaway profiling copy of the round-7 source (_r8p/) with a PT_SPLIT=1 host hook that encodes the trace dispatch and the combine pass into two separate command buffers, so each one's GPUStartTime/GPUEndTime pair is timed independently, and printed both. The same split showed the combine pass is pure bandwidth work (a 201 MB read of the 12-byte-per-sample buffer plus a 3 MB write), which is why attacking sample-buffer traffic was judged not worth it and all remaining effort went into the BVH walk itself.

Supporting cost breakdown from the same harness, for context: max-depth sweep gave trace_gpu_ms 5.82 (depth 1), 10.96 (2), 17.10 (3), 30.28 (12), and disabling the shadow-ray walk entirely gave 26.68 ms, so next-event-estimation shadow rays account for only about 3.65 ms (12%) — the dominant cost is closest-hit traversal ALU/latency.
